official_sources.title: Accuracy of OS Net, OSTN15 and OSGM15

verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 grid data is supplied in ASCII and GML-related form.
The GML file carries metadata including location, grid spacing and vertical reference information.
OS Terrain 50 ASCII values represent a raster grid.
Each OS Terrain 50 pixel is 50m by 50m.
A standard grid tile is 10km by 10km.
Height values are given to the nearest 0.1m.
OS Terrain 50 grid data has been verified to 4m RMSE.
OS Terrain 50 is suitable as a broad terrain reference rather than parcel-scale precision evidence.
OS Terrain 50 is designed for use in GIS and analytical/modelling workflows.
OS Net base-station standard errors are generally better than 0.008m in plan.
OS Net base-station standard errors are generally better than 0.020m in height.
OSTN15 defines OSGB36 National Grid in conjunction with OS Net stations.
OS describes OSTN15 transformation error as effectively negligible relative to GNSS positioning errors for modern use.
Agreement between OSTN15 and the old triangulation network is about 0.1m rms for Great Britain.
OSGM15 Great Britain regional height datum standard error is 0.008m, excluding GNSS heighting errors.
quality_effect: Keeps OS Terrain 50 as an independent coarse reference, preserves its 50m/4m-RMSE limits, and pins OSGB36/ODN transform uncertainty separately from EA LIDAR measurement uncertainty.
